solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: A Tory politician who has gone underground, perhaps literally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun (a country) but works as a verb, AVER.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: the hobby of exploring caves and potholes below ground.

entries.clue: Price of lettuce with Truss’s face attached (4)

indicatorNotes.face: a face is the front, so Truss's face is her first letter

blocks.note: cos is a variety of lettuce (romaine)
first letter of Truss

annotation.surface: A jibe at Liz Truss, the UK prime minister famously outlasted by a lettuce.
annotation.walkthrough: Liz Truss was briefly UK prime minister in 2022; a newspaper livestreamed a lettuce to see if it would outlast her, which is the joke behind the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the amount you must pay for something.

indicatorNotes.taking: taking time off: the T is taken away
indicatorNotes.off: time goes off, removed from the word

blocks.note: a valet is a gentleman's manservant
T = time, removed from the end

annotation.surface: A servant called Glen having a day off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glen' looks like the servant's name, but it is the definition: a glen is a valley.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name a valley, glen the Scottish word and the other the poetic one.

entries.clue: The shape of football pitch in playing field introducing confusion (9)

blocks.note: the rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field in Britain
a tangle is a confused muddle

annotation.surface: Chaos on the local playing field over the shape of the football pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain the rec, short for recreation ground, is a public park with playing fields.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a football pitch is one familiar instance of the four-right-angled shape.

blocks.note: L = left
the breadwinner is the one who earns

annotation.surface: A family's breadwinner has walked out and left the student to fend for themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a verb, 'walked out on', but is just the letter L.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: anyone studying is acquiring knowledge, one who learns.

entries.clue: Speak without restraint contributing to indefensible tripe (3,3)

indicatorNotes.contributing to: the answer's letters contribute to the phrase: they sit inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: Someone ranting and adding to a pile of indefensible nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: Tripe here is the surface's 'nonsense'; the answer straddles the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to hold nothing back, here in what you say.

blocks.note: used as it stands
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A ruling handed down by a court.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase; the definition is only the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a law passed by parliament is a formal decree, as an edict is.

entries.clue: Many signs of hesitation surrounded by common sense (8)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: the hesitation sounds go inside the word for common sense

blocks.note: nous is British slang for practical common sense
UM and ER, both sounds of hesitation, inside NO…US

annotation.surface: Lots of ums and ers from a person otherwise full of common sense.
annotation.walkthrough: Nous, from Greek, is informal British English for common sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe a large number of things.

indicatorNotes.about: the letters of CARED are moved about

blocks.note: a Red is a communist
anagram of CARED

annotation.surface: A left-wing activist campaigning to save a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' in the surface but asks for a rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one species of North American conifer.

blocks.note: so = very, as in 'so good'
licit means lawful

annotation.surface: A petition that is entirely above board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Petition' reads as a noun but is the verb: to ask formally.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both verbs mean to ask formally or earnestly for something.

entries.clue: Make it less bright, on reflection, lacking courage (5)

indicatorNotes.on reflection: a reflection shows things back to front

blocks.note: to dim something makes it less bright; read the phrase backwards

annotation.surface: Someone who turns the lights down because, thinking it over, they are shy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'having thought about it'; here it means the letters are mirrored.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone short of courage is fearful and shy.

entries.clue: Where to purchase delicious buffet ie pastries (10)

annotation.definitionNote: read as 'where to purchase delicious things'

indicatorNotes.buffet: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A buffet table of delicious pastries, and where you would buy them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' wants to be a spread of food; it is the verb meaning to batter.
annotation.definitionFit: The French cake shop sells pastries, so it is where you buy delicious things.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A green space surrounding the plains of Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it wants a container, but nothing is put inside anything.
annotation.definitionFit: Proper name: the great grassland of Tanzania and Kenya, famous for its migrations.

indicatorNotes.leaves: the female departs from the word

blocks.note: wayward = straying from the intended path
F = female, one F removed

annotation.surface: A wayward woman walking out, just as everyone expected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as foliage or departing; it removes one F from the phrase for wayward.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase is said when something goes without saying.

entries.clue: Suspect water vapour is associated with corrosion (8)

blocks.note: mist is fine water vapour
rust is corrosion of iron

annotation.surface: A chemistry note suspecting that damp causes corrosion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' reads as 'believe' in the surface but is the verb meaning to distrust.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to suspect a person is to doubt their honesty.

indicatorNotes.in: the circle goes in the iron

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is a circle, inside F…E

annotation.surface: A ring set within an iron edge.
annotation.walkthrough: Iron is FE, its chemical symbol, a very common crossword device.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a decorative edging on a rug or scarf, and by extension any outer edge.

entries.clue: Leader of Union aboard public transport getting a shock (6)

indicatorNotes.Leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.aboard: the U gets on board the tram

blocks.note: a tram is a street-running rail vehicle
first letter of Union, placed inside TRA…M
taken as it is

annotation.surface: A union boss on the bus or tram gets an unpleasant jolt.
annotation.walkthrough: The final A is the 'a' in 'a shock', shared between wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a deeply distressing experience that stays with you.

entries.clue: Climbing mountain with son and mother gives a bit of blood (6)

indicatorNotes.Climbing: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, backwards

blocks.note: an alp is a mountain, turned upwards
S = son
ma = mother

annotation.surface: A mountaineering family trip that ends with a blood test.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the mountain climbs; son and mother follow in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Part for whole: the pale yellow fluid carrying the cells is one component of blood.

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are arranged badly, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: The ninth man in the line-up is performing poorly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Badly' sits by 'failing' as though describing it, but it scrambles the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: said of a TV or machine working only fitfully, like a flickering light.

blocks.note: odd letters: B(r)A(m)B(l)E(s)

annotation.surface: A child discovered among the brambles, a fairy-tale foundling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in' suggests a hidden word, but no straight run works: every other letter is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal word for a baby or very young child, as in 'babe in arms'.

entries.clue: Report of unemployed person who is greatly admired (4)

indicatorNotes.Report of: a report is something heard, so go by sound

blocks.note: idle = without work

annotation.surface: A news story about a jobless man who is nevertheless much admired.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Report' reads as a news item; here it asks for a word that sounds the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a star or hero worshipped by fans.

entries.clue: Endless shortage of water is harsh (5)

indicatorNotes.Endless: both ends of the word are removed

blocks.note: a drought is a lack of rain; drop its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A never-ending drought makes life hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endless' reads as 'unending'; here it cuts both ends off the word for a dry spell.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe treatment that is severe or unkind.

blocks.note: he = a male person
N = new

annotation.surface: A man out with his new girlfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a girlfriend, which is where the surface points; here it is the feathered kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the domestic chicken, or any female bird.

entries.clue: Official waste abandoned next to road (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoned: abandoned means wild, unrestrained, so the letters run loose
indicatorNotes.next to: RD goes next to the rearranged letters

blocks.note: anagram of WASTE
RD is the abbreviation for road

annotation.surface: A council officer dealing with rubbish fly-tipped by the roadside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as dumped, fitting the waste; its job is 'wild', an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone appointed to manage an event, a race meeting or an estate.

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain is to hold, so the words hold the answer

blocks.note: the letters start at the end of the first word and run into the third

annotation.surface: Reviews of Toni Arthur, a British children's TV presenter and folk singer, performing abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: Toni Arthur presented the BBC children's show Play School in the 1970s; her name is there only to carry the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the three Baltic states.

blocks.note: used as it stands
to deal is to hand out cards

annotation.surface: A card dealer declaring themself flawless.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the wordplay reads straight through as a two-word sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: as good as it could possibly be, without fault.
